items.text: The universal $G$-torsor over a topos $S$
$S$ a topos, $B$ its category of sheaves, $G$ a group object of $B$.
Theory over $S$: topoi $X$ with a morphism $X\to S$, together with a torsor on $X$ under the inverse image of $G$.
Example: $S$ the classifying topos of rings — topoi with a sheaf of rings (ringed topoi).
T_G(X)=\{\text{torsors on }X\text{ under }G_X\}
Represent it: find $S'$ over $S$ and a torsor $P'$ under $G_{S'}$ such that
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Top}/S}(X,S')\longrightarrow T_G(X),\qquad f\mapsto f^{*}(P')
The universal $G$-torsor. Use: reduce to the universal case, where the topoi are explicit (Chern classes, crystalline classes).
Case $S$ = point: $G$ a group; $B_G$ = sets with $G$-action; functor left exact iff $X$ is a torsor.
Construction
\operatorname{Sh}(S')=B_G=\{\text{objects of }B\text{ with a (left) action of }G\}
Forgetful functor $B_G\to B$ is faithful and commutes with limits: $B_G$ is a topos.
p\colon S'\to S,\qquad p^{*}\colon B\to B_G,\ X\mapsto X\ \text{with trivial action}
Inverse image of the group: $\bar G$ = $G$ with trivial $G$-action.
Torsor: take $P@=G_s$, $G$ acting on $G$ by left translations.
P'\times\bar G\to P',\qquad (x,g)\mapsto xg\quad\text{(right translations = composition in }G)
Compatible with the left $G$-action because left and right translations commute.
Torsor: checked after the faithful exact forgetful functor ($G_s$ is a trivial torsor in $B$).
In $S'$ it is not trivial: a section would be invariant under left translations.
Universality: diagram of inverse images
\begin{CD} B @>{p^*}>> B_G\\ @V{q^*}VV @.\\ E @. \end{CD}
A torsor in $E$ under $q^*G$ $\leftrightarrow$ a functor $B_G\to E$ with the right exactness, triangle commuting up to isomorphism.
Y\in B_G\ \longmapsto\ X\times^{G}q^{*}(Y)\quad(\text{contracted product})
Composite $B_G\to E_G\to E$. Usually take $B=E$ (base change); torsors $\leftrightarrow$ sections of $B_G$.
Question from the room: other examples? $G$ a monoid — what does $B_G$ classify?
Example : locally free modules of rank $n$
Ringed topos $X$ (over the classifying topos of rings); $\mathcal O_X$-modules locally free of rank $n$.
Want constructions (relative group schemes, cohomology, Chern classes): go to the universal case.
A stack: objects glue (2-descent for epimorphic families). Objects locally isomorphic to a given one are classified by torsors under its automorphism sheaf.
\{\text{modules locally}\simeq\mathcal O_X^n\}\ \simeq\ \{\text{torsors under }\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal O_X^n)=GL_n(\mathcal O_X)\}
Universal ring: $S$ = presheaves on affine schemes of finite type over $\mathbb Z$; ring $\mapsto$ underlying set.
S\ \text{classifying topos of rings},\quad G=GL_n(\mathcal O),\quad B_G=\text{universal topos for rank }n\text{ locally free modules}
If the sheaf of rings is local: factor through the subtopos with the Zariski topology instead of the chaotic one.
Strictly local (Henselian): a still finer topology; the universal topos shrinks with the requirements.
Example : locally constant objects of rank $n$
Locally constant objects: $E\mapsto$ full subcategory of $E$ — not representable (not stable under direct limits; fails for totally disconnected spaces).
Locally constant of order $n$ (an $n$-sheeted covering of the final object): not algebraic either — sets of cardinal $n$ are not stable under filtering limits.
Finite coverings of order $n$ only — otherwise $X$ splits as a sum.
I\ \text{locally}\simeq I_n=\{1,\dots,n\},\qquad \operatorname{Aut}(I_n)=S_n\ \text{(constant sheaf)}
\{\text{such }I\}\ \simeq\ \{\text{torsors under }S_n\}\quad(\text{isomorphisms only})
Same caveat for locally free modules: only isomorphisms between objects; same objects, different homomorphisms.
\text{universal topos with a locally constant object of rank }n=B_{S_n}
Example : rings with $n$ connected components
Spectrum connected: two orthogonal idempotents with sum $1$ ⟹ one of them is $0$. Makes sense in every topos (a subtopos of the classifying topos of rings).
Exactly $n$ components: not a theory (not stable under filtering limits). Notion: $A$ = product of $n$ non-zero 0-connected rings, canonical.
Modified morphisms: those inducing isomorphisms on the sets of components,
\pi_0^{!}(A)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\pi_0^{!}(B)\qquad(\text{ring structure taken into account, }\sim\pi_0\operatorname{Spec})
Correct description: a product locally; the index set is a twisted object of rank $n$.
Data: a locally constant object $I$ of rank $n$ (an $n$-sheeted covering $X'\to X$) and a 0-connected ring $A_0$ over $I$.
A=f_{*}(A_0),\qquad f\colon X'\to X
Fully faithful with morphisms inducing isomorphisms on $\pi_0$; $I$ and $A_0$ determined up to unique isomorphism.
With enough points: all stalks have spectra with exactly $n$ components.
Category of such rings $\simeq$ {$n$-sheeted covering $I$, plus a 0-connected ring over $I$ with non-zero connected stalks}.
Universal $I$ (isomorphisms only) and universal ring over $S$-topos: product with the topos of the universal ring.
$n$-rings: locally exactly $n$ orthogonal idempotents summing to $1$, not further divisible.
X\to B_{S_n}\ \text{gives }I\text{ on }X;\qquad I_n\ \text{universal }n\text{-fold covering}
Then: all ways to give a 0-connected ring over $I_n$ …
